title: A user variable named after a libm function (fmax) makes the generated C fail to compile
root_cause: The libm/libc surface was missing from is_reserved_c_ident, so `double fmax;` collided with math.h's declaration.

title: A user def named fmod makes compiled mod(7, 3) call the user's function (10 in C, 1 interpreted)
root_cause: The lowering emits fmod/fmin/fmax/tgamma for builtins, and a user def of that name shared the C callee namespace.

title: A rank-5 array panics the compiler instead of giving a diagnostic
root_cause: Ranks above 4 hit an unhandled case in the compiler rather than a reported limit.

title: Two modules defining one def run in the interpreter but fail to compile
root_cause: The interpreter let a later def replace an earlier one of the same name; the C backend refused the duplicate.

title: Indexing a function registry infers a number, so a def returning apply needs an explicit -> Arr
root_cause: Registry elements were inferred as numbers, so apply never learned its callee's return kind.

title: A top-level apply result is left undeclared in the generated C
root_cause: Same cause as the registry inference bug: apply's result kind was unknown, so no declaration was emitted.

title: A def that reads global k and then assigns local k gives C that clang rejects, or a silent difference between engines
root_cause: The interpreter read the global before the local existed while the C declared one local for the whole def.

title: both-engines.sh stops the sweep when clang fails on one program
test blocks share one scope with top-level code, so a test binding p collides with a top-level p of another type
root_cause: The C backend infers one type per identifier per program; there is no scope frame per test block.

title: A def with no call site gets Num parameters and fails far away ("argument 2 should be a array")
root_cause: An uncalled def's untyped parameters defaulted to real numbers; it is now left out when some other guess types it.

title: The wasm engine runs about a thousand times slower than native on the same program (lib/linalg + schur + are: 0.00 s vs 1.18 s)
C array indexing has no bounds checks: an out-of-bounds read or write runs on where the interpreter stops
root_cause: The C accessors indexed memory directly; they now go through viv_ix with the interpreter's message and location.

title: The interpreter reads a function registry at index -1 as element 0
root_cause: The registry index path skipped the bounds check the array path had.

title: C reads a[5] on a 2 x 3 array as a flat index where the interpreter stops on the rank
root_cause: The C accessors did not compare the number of indices with the array's rank.

title: cos(x) next to sin(x) gives a different last bit at -O0 and -O2, so eig_sym and the fft differ between debug and release engines
root_cause: An optimizer merged the two calls into one sincos with a different rounding; both are now kept as two libm calls.

title: The "N assertions FAILED" summary goes to different streams in the two engines
A def passed as an argument whose result is a complex array times a real array is typed as a real array
root_cause: Arithmetic with one operand not typed yet and a real array on the other answered real in the first fixpoint.

title: conj(v) @ transpose(v) in a test block, with v returned by a def, is typed as a real array
root_cause: transpose of an untyped value, and @ with an untyped side, answered real before the def's return type arrived.

title: linspace(0.0, STEPS, n) with STEPS a global set from a def's result makes STEPS an array
root_cause: Inference took linspace's untyped arguments to be arrays.

title: In C an index expression is evaluated before the accessor counts indices, so a nested a[b[9]] on the wrong-rank array reports its own error where the interpreter reports the rank
root_cause: The C computes the index arguments before the rank check in the accessor; the interpreter counts first.

title: Solver run-time errors in C (certificates, eig_herm, cholesky, tridiag_solve, take/put/slab/roll) use C's own wording and no location
root_cause: Only lin_solve and the symmetric eigensolvers route through viv_solver_fail with the interpreter's words.

title: Run-time errors from the direct wasm backend carry no location
root_cause: run-wasm.mjs reports the message alone; the wasm module has no location table.

title: The browser expands #! use in JS and hands viv.wasm the expanded text, so the site shows error lines of the expanded program
root_cause: www/src/lib/uses.js expands modules itself instead of registering a composite source as the native driver does.

title: and/or evaluate both sides in the interpreter and wasm, so a guard like j >= 0 and a[j] > 0 stops them but runs natively
root_cause: Only the C short-circuited; the interpreter and the wasm backend evaluated the right side unconditionally.

title: A call to an unknown function in a branch never taken runs in the interpreter and is refused by the compile
root_cause: viv run interpreted without running the compiler's front end, so only the compile saw the error.

title: A loop variable later assigned an array runs in the interpreter and is refused by the compile
root_cause: Same cause: the interpreter skipped the front end's type check.

title: A top-level variable named like a def from a module runs in the interpreter and fails in cc
root_cause: The two names became one C identifier; the interpreter keeps variables and defs apart.

title: Deep recursion overflows the interpreter's stack near 2000 calls where the C goes on
root_cause: Each engine was limited by its own native stack; there was no shared recursion limit.

title: deriv differentiates exp, sqrt, pow by the builtin's rule even when the program defines its own def of that name
root_cause: deriv matched builtin names before user defs, so it differentiated a function the program never calls.

title: A notebook cell restarts rand() at the default seed, so a cell draws other numbers than viv run does at the same point
root_cause: interp::run_cell kept functions and globals across cells but not the generator's state.

title: The direct wasm backend emits no rank or bounds checks: an out-of-bounds index reads or writes linear memory
root_cause: The backend was written against the IR before index nodes carried a location, so it emitted no checks.

title: engines/dft-bands prints BANDRES 9.88458e-07 interpreted and 9.88432e-07 native
max(a, b) or min(a, b) inside a def whose arguments are typed only by a later call site is typed as a number
root_cause: max, min and negation with an untyped argument answered "a number" in the first fixpoint and the def's return type never changed.

title: sort sorts in place and returns a number, so return sort(w) fails as a type error somewhere else
root_cause: sort's value was a placeholder 0 rather than refused.

title: sort orders -0.0, +0.0 and values next to a NaN differently in C and the interpreter
root_cause: C used qsort; the interpreter and wasm used Rust's stable sort_by treating NaN as equal to everything.

title: show of an expression, a field or an element (show g.W, show w[0]) prints no label
Complex division differs in the last bit between C and the interpreter
root_cause: C used double complex `/` with a platform-chosen scaling, the interpreter the textbook formula; both are now Smith's algorithm.

title: eig_sym orders eigenvectors of equal eigenvalues differently in C and the interpreter
root_cause: The C runtime's exchange sort was not stable.

title: x ^ 2 or print(u0) with an operand not typed yet fixes an array from a def as a number
root_cause: pow's scalar case and print's default fixed the type before the def's return type arrived.

title: -c and f(a) ^ 2.0 of an array a def returned fail to build
root_cause: Negation and ^ answered "a number" for an untyped operand instead of waiting.

title: The C backend does not check array shapes: u * v of lengths 3 and 2 and a mismatched @ print a result
root_cause: C's elementwise and matmul operations had no shape check; they now go through viv_arr_chk.

title: max(-0.0, 0.0) is -0.0 in wasm and 0.0 in the interpreter and C
root_cause: Rust's f64::max compiles to a compare in wasm, and the C library's fmax tie of zeros is platform-defined; both now use vmath::fmax/fmin.

title: Negating a complex array loses the sign of a zero imaginary part in C and wasm
root_cause: The lowering scaled by -1 + 0i instead of negating both parts.

title: erf(inf), erf(-inf) and gamma(inf) are NaN
root_cause: The formulas took -inf + inf and inf * 0 where x^2 overflows.

title: gamma is about 1e-15 off relative (gamma(3.0) is 6.000000000000007)
root_cause: Lanczos approximation with g = 7 is not correctly rounded.

title: spectrum_sym or eig_sym of a matrix with a NaN panics the interpreter and exits 0 in C
root_cause: The sort of eigenvalues hit `unreachable` on a NaN; the C ran on.

title: lin_solve of a singular matrix stops with different words in the interpreter and C
root_cause: The C wrote its own message before the program's output instead of the interpreter's located error after it.

title: A real array plus a complex number does not build, and sum takes no complex array
Native show of a tie prints 7.89030e+06 on macOS where the interpreter and wasm print 7.8903e+06
root_cause: The C runtime used the platform's printf %g; it now uses Viv's own formatter.

title: Steps inside code the autodiff pass inlines are named block_forward/attn_norm by the interpreter and gpt_forward/attn_norm by C and wasm
root_cause: step_def_name in lower.rs took the first step's def for the whole generated body.

title: a[::s] with the step in a variable is empty in every engine
root_cause: The array slicer read the parser's slice kind 4 (start left out, step sign unknown) as a range ending at 0.

title: A variable named acct, index, read or write is a C compile error
root_cause: unistd.h, strings.h, signal.h and select.h names were missing from the libc collision list.

title: A global named NAN (or another C macro or keyword name) does not compile to C
root_cause: is_reserved_c_ident did not cover math.h/complex.h macros or C keywords.

title: A user def main breaks the C backend
root_cause: main was not in the reserved-name list, so the user's def collided with the C entry point.

title: Unpacking a Bool from a tuple return inside a test block fails ("t_b is a number but is assigned a boolean")
Complex slice assignment refuses a real 0.0
tools/three-engines.sh dft cannot run: dft's check files compile only as preludes
weft's symbolic diff_u returns 0 for pow with a non-constant exponent and for any other call
root_cause: lang/weft/src/compile.rs falls through to 0 instead of refusing what it cannot differentiate.

title: The vendored pow does j += n<<20 with n negative, undefined behavior in C
root_cause: A left shift of a negative int; replaced by n * 2^20, the same bits.

title: A loop calling keys(m) or values(m) leaks 128 bytes a call in C
root_cause: The C emitter's own list of allocating calls missed viv_map_keys and viv_map_values.

title: A while loop whose condition allocates keeps 512 bytes a pass in C and wasm
root_cause: An allocating condition did not make the loop count as allocating, so no arena release was emitted.

title: Maps made in a def or a loop pass are never freed until the run ends
root_cause: Maps lived outside the arena, so returning from a def or ending a pass released nothing.

title: A parallel for whose body allocates grows without bound (a def called 200 times reached 82 MB on 8 threads)
root_cause: Passes of a parallel for did not release their allocations on the thread that ran them.

title: viv lens check panics (index out of bounds in infer_signatures) on a program that defines one def twice with different arities
A fractional, NaN or infinite index is truncated in every engine (v[2.9999999] reads v[2], v[0/0] reads v[0])
root_cause: Indices were converted with a truncating cast; in release C a NaN index was undefined behavior.

title: zeros(65536, 65537) wraps to 65,536 elements in C and A[1, 0] writes past the block; wasm counts in 32 bits and prints a different size
root_cause: The C runtime multiplied dimensions into an int and did not check calloc; the wasm runtime counted in 32 bits.

title: clip with a -0.0 bound gives +0.0 in C under clang -O2 on arm64
root_cause: Clang compiled clip's select into fmaxnm once the bound was an inlined -0.0 constant.

title: has(M, key) in a def on a module map makes the map a local of the def, so a string key is refused
root_cause: The backward pass of a call learned the module's map as a local of the def; m[k] = v already left it to the global.

title: sol = solve A @ x = b marks x assigned, so a later integrate x^2 from 0 to 1 is refused as having no free variable
root_cause: Any name before an = inside a phrase counted as assigned, not only a name that starts a statement.

title: The browser and the wasm runner drop a program's output when it stops with an error
root_cause: The wasm entry points returned only the error, discarding what the program had printed.

title: return 1 in a recursive -> Int def is refused as a number
root_cause: The recursion limit's rewrite held each return value in an undeclared temporary that defaulted to a number.

title: A def that can reach its end without a return gives 0 in the interpreter and wasm and an undefined value in C
root_cause: The C emitted no return at a reachable end; for a string that was a pointer into unowned memory.

title: wasm keep helpers skip enum fields of records, freeing nodes an array of records still holds
root_cause: Keep helpers of records that reach an enum did not take the release mark for enum fields.

title: In the interpreter a function-valued parameter f called as f(x) runs the global def f when one exists; C and wasm call the argument (-99 vs 2)
root_cause: The interpreter resolves a call by global def name before local function values.

title: sorted(v) of an array of numbers is refused without key=
print and show refuse a whole complex array
A matrix literal with a complex element is refused; only a vector literal promotes
n: Int = 2 ^ 62 (and 2 ^ 10) is refused as a number assigned to an Int, against int_enum.md D7
q = p of a record shares its array fields: q.v[0] = 9.0 changes p.v
A lambda that captures a local is refused by the interpreter too, not only by the compiled backends
The pseudocode view drops a closing parenthesis and puts an intent line under the wrong step
viv debt misses a dead def that viv lens needed reports, and shows 0 callers for a def the top level calls
viv lens needed prints a count of unparsed files over the whole repository, whatever paths it is given
Messages read "this is a array", "1 phrases", and viv arch report prints "ran 3 defs (150% of those loaded)"
On an Int overflow stop the interpreter prints the PASS lines before the error and the compiled engines do not
enumerate(e, 1) gives Num indices and for i to len(xs) makes i a Num, so return Some(i) into an Int? is refused
The fast build included <Accelerate/Accelerate.h>, whose MacTypes.h types (`wide`, `Fixed`, `Boolean`) collided with a program's own variable names (lib/optim's `wide`)
root_cause: system headers in generated C; the BLAS and LAPACK prototypes are now declared in the C itself

title: With -ffp-contract=fast-honor-pragmas the fast build did not contract: vmath.c's own `#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF` came after the fast pragma and turned contraction off for the rest of the file
root_cause: pragma order in the preamble; the fast pragma now follows vmath.c

title: lang/viv/examples geomopt_water and scf_water_631gd stop in the interpreter with 'interpreter step budget exceeded', so tools/three-engines.sh lang/viv/examples fails (C and wasm run them; same on main 9b055e2)

A test's `assert_true(ok)` made `ok` a number before the comparison assigned to it was typed (the comparison read a value unpacked from a def whose return type arrived later), so the program was refused: "`ok` is a number but is assigned a boolean"
root_cause: lower.rs infer: an untyped argument of assert_true defaulted to a number; assert_true is now overloaded (a boolean or a number) like print

title: `d: Int = 2 if c else 1`: the if-expression's hidden variable takes the first branch's literal as a number, so the annotated Int binding is refused (`viv__if` is a number but is assigned an Int); an if statement with the same literals works

An Int loop variable counted again to a literal bound (`for i to n` with n an Int, then `for i to 3`) compiled to invalid wasm: the counter was converted to f64 for the variable's i64 local (CompileError at instantiate); the interpreter and C ran it
found_by: npb (NPB EP and IS ports, three-engines)
root_cause: wasm_backend.rs For: the conversion followed the bound's type, not the variable's

title: A loop that appends records holding arrays is quadratic in the C runtime: viv_arena_release_kept compares every array filed since the loop began with every kept array at each iteration (benzene cc-pVDZ's 1,176-pair ERI store: 1.46 s, against 8 ms built by halves)
root_cause: lang/viv/src C runtime: the kept check is a linear search of viv_kept for each arena entry above the loop's mark; enum nodes already avoid it with a pass mark

title: extend(a, b) refuses arrays of records (`extend` joins two real vectors), so joining two [T] needs a comprehension

In the notebook's cell-by-cell session (interp::run_cell, viv_run_cell) `int(x)` gives a number, so `H = int_zeros(3)` then `H[1] = int(n)` stops with 'an Int array holds Ints, and this is a number'; the whole program runs
root_cause: run_cell_keeping builds its Interp with fresh_interp, whose IntSites (the int() calls and literals the lowering decides are Ints) are empty; run sets them from parse_items_diag. The cell and the prefix are parsed separately with spans relative to each, so the sites cannot simply be merged

title: lang/viv/tests/records.rs failed now and then under `cargo test --workspace`: two tests run the same program with the tag `roundtrip` at once, share one temporary directory, and one removes it while the other compiles, so the other prints nothing
root_cause: the test helper named its directory by process id and tag only; it now adds a per-call counter

title: The C of a checked access quotes the access's whole source line in viv_sites, once per access, so a generated def with long lines and many accesses makes a C file quadratic in the line length: 20,776-term contraction kernels written one row to a line gave 60 MB of C that clang had not compiled after 7 minutes
root_cause: site_row renders the interpreter's location text (file:line:col, the line, the caret) per distinct column; rows differ only in the caret, so the table could hold each line once and the caret column per row

title: `viv features --usage` reports a stencil's shifted slices (jacobi-1d `A[0:N - 2] + A[1:N - 1] + A[2:N]`, fdtd-2d, heat-3d) and a matrix's column slices as `flat-params` (W2, parameters kept in one flat vector): a false positive on every stencil

A function value forwarded through two defs is lost: every_rule(func) -> report(func, left_rect) -> integrate(func, ..., rule) -> rule(f, ...) fails with '`left_rect` expects a function for parameter(s) `f`'; with one level of forwarding it runs
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: defun.rs rewrote every_rule in place before its one call site specialized it; in that copy `func` is a plain parameter, so report and integrate were specialized with `f` unknown as a function and the call `rule(f, ...)` was refused. The copy is dead (every call of every_rule was specialized), but its errors were reported. Errors now record the def they were found in, and errors in, and copies of, defs nothing reaches are dropped.
repro: def left_rect(f, x, h) { return f(x) }  ...  def every_rule(func) { report(func, left_rect) }; every_rule(cube)
note: rosetta id B092 (numerical_integration); renumbered B200

title: exp(1.0) prints 2.7182818284590455, one ulp above the nearest double to e (2.718281828459045, which CPython's math.exp(1) and math.e give)
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: Viv's libm exp is musl's fdlibm exp, within one ulp but not correctly rounded.
repro: print(fmt(exp(1.0)))
note: rosetta id B094 (calculating_the_value_of_e); renumbered B201. A correctly rounded exp is built and held to its C twin bit for bit (lang/viv/src/vmath/exp_cr.rs, viv_exp_cr in tools/vmath/vmath_tail.c; 0 wrong of 400,000 inputs against Python's decimal, tests/vmath.rs exp_cr_is_correctly_rounded; about 1.8x musl's cost), and identical in all three engines, but `exp` does not call it yet: switching moves lib/minpack's Meyer problem (factor 10, which stops at maxfev) off the Fortran oracle's trajectory (x differs by 25%), and changes the exp-dependent counts two posts state (2026-09-24-two-integral-families: 2492 bit-identical integrals become 2483; 2026-09-25-gauss-legendre...: tanh-sinh's error 3.1e-15 against its stated 3e-15). The owner decides. Meanwhile the constant `e` (crate::stdlib) is the double nearest e.

title: The literal `[[]]` is a 1 x 0 matrix in the interpreter and C but a rank-1 empty array in wasm: print(one(0)) prints [[]] vs [], shape [1, 0] vs [0]
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: The direct wasm backend called the runtime's vrt_lit(width, rows, cols) with cols = 0 for a rank-1 literal, and vrt_lit read cols = 0 as rank 1, so an r x 0 literal came out rank 1. A rank-1 literal now passes cols = -1.
repro: def one(m) { if m == 0 { return [[]] } return [[1.0, 2.0]] }; print(one(0)); print(shape(one(0)))
note: rosetta id B096 (combinations); renumbered B202

title: A zero-pad format flag is silently ignored: fmt(-1.5, "06.2f") and f"{x:06.2f}" give " -1.50" (Python: "-01.50"); fmt(2.0, "05d") gives "    2" (Python: "00002")
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: printfmt::parse_spec read the 0 as the first digit of the width. Specs now follow Python's grammar: the zero flag sets the fill to 0 and the alignment to = (between the sign and the digits); fill, alignment, sign, grouping, %, E/F/G are formats too, carried to C and wasm in the kind word (Fmt::word) and applied by printfmt::finish and its C twin viv_numfin. 574 number cases and 97 Int and string cases match CPython in all three engines.
note: rosetta id B091 (formatted_numeric_output); renumbered B203

title: An if-expression mixing an integer literal and an Int (`return 0 if n == 0 else n` in a `-> Int` def) is refused with an error naming the compiler's temporary `viv__if1`
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: The parser writes the if-expression's value as a hidden variable assigned in each branch; inference typed it from its first assignment, the literal 0, as a number. An integer literal assigned to that variable is now held back until the other branch's type is known, and `x: T = a if c else b` declares the hidden variable a T.
repro: def f(n: Int) -> Int { return 0 if n == 0 else n }
note: rosetta id B095 (least_common_multiple); renumbered B204

title: int(x) bound to a name without a type is a number, though the Int diagnostic says int(x) makes an Int: s = int(2.0); f(s) with f(n: Int) is refused
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: int(...) adapts only in an Int position (D3), and `s = int(2.0)` is not one. A variable whose every assignment is an Int (int(...), a literal, Int arithmetic of such variables) and one of them int(...) is now an Int (lower/ints.rs infer_int_vars); the refusal of a number for an Int parameter now says how to make one.
repro: def f(n: Int) -> Int { return n }; s = int(2.0); print(f(s))
note: rosetta shard s01, bug s01-03

title: Two string literals side by side are accepted and the second is silently dropped: "a" "b" gives "a", and """abc""" gives ""
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: The parser read one string literal as a primary and the expression ended there; the next literal was left as a statement of its own, a docstring, and dropped. """abc""" lexed as "", "abc", "". Adjacent literals now join (an f-string among them by +), and the lexer reads triple-quoted strings; a triple-quoted f-string is refused.
repro: t = "a" "b"; print(t)
note: rosetta shard s01, bug s01-02 (silent wrong result)

title: An empty list annotated [Str] is a number array in the interpreter: used: [Str] = []; "a" in used stops with '`in` looks for a number in an array', where C and wasm print false
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: The lowering makes [] an empty list of strings where one is declared; the interpreter keeps [] an empty real array until a string is appended, and its `in` read that as a number array. `in` of a string in an empty array is now false.
repro: used: [Str] = []; print("a" in used)
note: rosetta shard s01, bug s01-04

title: A record field cannot name a record declared later in the file: record Box { item: Thing } before record Thing gives 'unknown type Thing'
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: build_records resolved each record's fields against the records declared before it, and the C typedefs were written in declaration order. Both now follow record_order: each record after the records its fields name (a record that holds itself is still refused).
repro: record Box { item: Thing }; record Thing { n: Num }
note: rosetta shard s01, bug s01-05

title: A record field typed Map refuses a map with string keys, which a Map parameter accepts: 'field m of R is a map but this value is a map with string keys'
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: A Map field was settled to a map of numbers when the record was declared; a Map parameter's kinds are inferred from its uses. A Map field is now an open field: the record literals that build it give it its kinds, and it settles after inference.
repro: record R { m: Map }; m = map(); m["a"] = 1; r = R { m: m }
note: rosetta shard s01, bug s01-01

title: tests/records.rs: two tests pass the tag "shared" to run(), which used one scratch directory per process and tag, so parallel tests overwrote each other's r.c/r and interpreter_runs_records_as_c_does failed at random (NotFound)
found_by: gate-cache warm full gate (cargo-test); also seen on gpt-phrases
root_cause: scratch directory named by pid and tag only; fixed with a per-call counter in the name

title: An error in a --use file was shown at a line of the whole program text under the main program's name: the export prototype's ecut = -1 error at dft/pwdft_it.viv:253 was reported as report.viv:1231, and the C's location table for dft/ named dft/si_it_check.viv:250 for dft/pw_common.viv:114
root_cause: read_preludes concatenated the --use files into a prefix of the text and source_map recorded no origin for it, so every span in it resolved to source 0, named after the main program; the prefix is now a list of parts, each a piece of the composite source pointing into that file's own loaded map

title: Built with GCC 15 at -O2 -ffp-contract=off on aarch64, complex array products (viv_carr_had, viv_carr_scale) rounded differently from clang's and the interpreter's: 121 of 256 products of a test program, and every exported pwdft material's result hash
root_cause: GCC's loop vectorizer pattern-matches a complex multiply written in real arithmetic into FCMLA, a fused multiply-add, without regard to -ffp-contract=off; the runtime's complex loops are now optimize("no-tree-loop-vectorize") in an exact GCC build

title: `viv build` keeps a module in the program's unit, and emits the whole program again for each such module, when the program has an enum global named like a record field the module reads (`o.method` in lib/hf, `method = Method.Rhf` in the program): study/ports/pyscf/vivscf.viv spent 28 s in `--split` instead of 5 s and compiled lib/hf's five SCF modules with the program every time
found_by: vivscf (study/ports/pyscf/vivscf.viv, the PySCF port as one program with parameters)
root_cause: emit_split collected what a unit's functions reference with c_idents, which counts member names (`o.method`, `p->tag`) as identifiers; a member named like a program global pulled in the global's type, and an enum type is a program declaration, so the unit was refused. c_refs skips a word right after `.` or `->`.

title: `viv export --reports` wrote `print("RESULT x 0", fmt(x))` for a Bool result, and `fmt` takes numbers only, so tools/export/check.py could not compile the native or interpreted run of any program with a Bool result (vivscf's `converged`)
root_cause: report_viv handled Ty::Bool with Ty::Num; a Bool result now prints 1 or 0 from an if

title: `viv export` refused a parameter whenever any def of the program's files assigned a variable of the same name, imports included: vivscf's `method` and `atoms` were refused because lib/hf's `scf_result` (`method = setup.method`) and `mol_enuc` (`atoms = mol.atoms`) have locals so named

title: `viv export` refused a parameter as "read before this assignment" when its name appeared as a word anywhere above it outside comments, such as `basis` in `from basis.basis import Basis` or a record field of a spliced-in module
root_cause: the check matched words in the text (mentions); it now walks the parsed top-level statements before the assignment for a variable read of the name

title: viv export refused a parameter whose name is a local of a def in an imported module: SPACING was first H, and lib/skyrme/skyrme's skyrme_energy has a local H, so the export said 'the parameter `H` is assigned inside `skyrme_energy`'; minimal: a module def `g` with `H = x * N` and a program parameter H
root_cause: assemble scans every def of each file as load_text returns it, imports spliced in; import resolution renames a module's top-level names but not its defs' locals, so a module's local shares the program's name. A module's defs cannot assign the program's globals, so the scan should cover the program's own text only (the units load_text's map says came from the manifest's file). Duplicate of B262 (found the same day on branch vivscf-export): its fix reads a def's assignment as the def's local and refuses it only when no top level assigns the parameter, which covers a module's def; the regression test exports a program whose imported def has a local H beside a parameter H

title: viv export's exact-bits report (--reports, used by tools/export/check.py) prints a Bool result with fmt(), which refuses a boolean, so check.py cannot build the native or interpreted run of a program with a Bool result; skyrmehf's CONVERGED is a Num 0/1 instead
root_cause: report_viv groups Ty::Bool with Ty::Num and writes `fmt(NAME)`; a Bool needs `fmt(1.0 if NAME else 0.0)` or its own print. Duplicate of B261 (found the same day on branch vivscf-export, fixed there); skyrmehf's CONVERGED is a Bool again (lib/skyrme/skyrmehf.viv) and its hash is unchanged

title: viv export's 'read before this assignment' check counts a parameter's name in an imported module's ### docstring: lib/skyrme/skyrme's header text 'this module's MIX, E_TOL and MAX_ITER' refused MAX_ITER
root_cause: mentions() strips # comments but reads every other line of the spliced text, the module's fenced text included, and the module's text precedes the program's; import resolution renames the module's code but not the words of its fence. Fixed by B263's change, made the same day on branch vivscf-export: the check walks the parsed top-level statements before the assignment for a read of the variable, and a ### block is not a statement

title: viv export's errors in an imported module's text are shown under the program's file name with the spliced text's line number: skyrme_energy's `H = ...` (lib/skyrme/skyrme.viv) was reported at lib/skyrme/skyrmehf.viv:422, a 98-line file
root_cause: assemble's located() takes the unit's manifest path and the spliced text; it does not map the line through the source map load_text returns (the maps main.rs keeps for export_compile). Now export::assemble_mapped takes each file's source map from main.rs, and a refusal is rendered through it, so the line is the module's own (prog/mm.viv:6:5)

title: viv lens check, viv explain and viv lens coverage refuse a keyword argument to an imported def that viv run accepts: `from m.mm import f` then `f(1.0, b=3.0)` runs and passes, and the lens tools stop with 'unknown keyword argument `b=`', which also fails the coverage ratchet for the whole directory
root_cause: the lens tools parse the program's file without its imports spliced in, so the parser's def_sigs has no signature for an imported def and takes it for a builtin without keyword arguments; skyrmehf calls skyrme_hf positionally instead. Now parse_keeping_rungs passes the signatures of the defs a module imports by name (crate::used_sigs, from the module texts expand_uses remembered) to the parser, which treats them as defs of the text

title: `zv, zpv = f(z)` with f's complex results found late (over lib/zfunc), then `abs(zv)`, failed to compile: "`zv` is a number but is assigned a complex number" (type cannot change)
root_cause: callee_param_ty typed an unknown argument of abs (and exp, sqrt, log, sin, cos, tan) as a number in every inference pass; lib/zfunc's result types are found only in the pass that defaults indexing, after abs had typed zv. Those functions take complex numbers too, so they now say "a number" only in the last pass, once every other type is settled

title: `viv features` and the reference name the complex type `Cplx`, and the compiler took only `Complex` in an annotation: `def f(z: Cplx)` stopped with "unknown type `Cplx`"
root_cause: resolve_type matched the name Complex only; it takes Cplx too (unless a record of that name is declared)

title: viv export wrote a parameter or result into a C struct under its lowercased name without checking C's keywords or the struct's own fields: deck_param = "case" gave `int case;` and C that did not compile
root_cause: parse_manifest checks a name against C identifier syntax and Python's keywords only, not C's keywords (case, double, int, ...) or the generated struct fields (given, on_line, ctx; have, ntests, tests, error_kind, log). Worked around in plasma/vlasov.export.toml with deck_param = "setup". A fix (a C_KEYWORDS and a reserved-field list checked in parse_manifest, with cases in export::tests) was written and tested on branch vlasov, then withdrawn so the export fixes stay on export-rel

title: A def that no code calls, whose untyped parameter is used as an array and which calls another def, fails to compile with 'expected an array ... this is a number': `def mx_w(th) { return [th, 1.0 - th] }` and `def mx(f, s) { n = len(f)\n w = mx_w(s)\n return n + len(w) }`. A module whose only caller of such a def is its own test block compiles alone and fails when imported, since an import drops the tests
exp(1.0) prints 2.7182818284590455, one ulp above the nearest double to e (2.718281828459045, which CPython's math.exp(1) and math.e give)
found_by: rosetta study (first 100 tasks), fixed on branch fix-w1
root_cause: Viv's libm exp is musl's fdlibm exp, within one ulp but not correctly rounded.
repro: print(fmt(exp(1.0)))
note: rosetta id B094 (calculating_the_value_of_e); renumbered B201. A correctly rounded exp is built and held to its C twin bit for bit (lang/viv/src/vmath/exp_cr.rs, viv_exp_cr in tools/vmath/vmath_tail.c; 0 wrong of 400,000 inputs against Python's decimal, tests/vmath.rs exp_cr_is_correctly_rounded; about 1.8x musl's cost), and identical in all three engines, but `exp` does not call it yet: switching moves lib/minpack's Meyer problem (factor 10, which stops at maxfev) off the Fortran oracle's trajectory (x differs by 25%), and changes the exp-dependent counts two posts state (2026-09-24-two-integral-families: 2492 bit-identical integrals become 2483; 2026-09-25-gauss-legendre...: tanh-sinh's error 3.1e-15 against its stated 3e-15). The owner decides. Meanwhile the constant `e` (crate::stdlib) is the double nearest e. Switched for release 0.0.1 on branch export-rel (owner decision 2026-10-07): `exp` is exp_cr in every engine, extended to the subnormal results (x <= -708) and the last binade before overflow, which were musl's and not correctly rounded there; tools/vmath/check_exp.py: 0 wrong of 2,025,786 inputs against mpmath, three engines identical. The posts and MINPACK's Meyer problem were re-checked on the switch (design/release-0.0.1.md).

title: `viv export` of a kernel collection whose files hold defs alone (no constants, no test blocks) wrote C that does not compile: the C backend writes no `main` for a program with no top level, and the collection's init calls `viv_program_main`, which `#define main` would have named
found_by: pyviv (vivlang's import hook on a one-def module)
root_cause: export_kernels::entry assumed every program has a top level; K1's files all have test blocks, so it never met one without.

title: `viv export` refused a kernel collection with an array argument whose program makes no array of its own (`def total(a: Arr) -> Num` summing in a loop): 'internal: an array argument, and the runtime has no viv_arr_new'
root_cause: export_kernels::entry copied every array argument with the runtime's viv_arr_new, which the C backend emits only when the program allocates an array. The entry now lends read-only arguments and, when the runtime has no viv_arr_new, copies the others into blocks of its own freed after the call.

title: `viv export` (and vivlang's import) of a module that takes `grad` of a def calling an imported def failed: "`grad` has no adjoint for `sq` with an argument that depends on the differentiated value", though `viv run` of the same module works
root_cause: The export reads each file alone (its imports not spliced in) for its defs' signatures, through viv::parse, which ends with the grad rewrite; with the imported defs missing, the rewrite took `sq` for a builtin without an adjoint. The export now reads files with parse_before_grad, the same pipeline stopped before the rewrite.
repro: aa.viv: def sq(x: Num) -> Num { return x * x }; bb.viv: from aa import sq / def w(x: Num) -> Num { return sq(x) } / def g(x: Num) -> Num { return grad(w, x) }; viv export --infer bb.viv -o out

title: `grad` of a def with a counted loop over an Int bound (`for k from 1 to N`, N: Int) does not compile: "`viv__ad_n188` is an Int but is assigned a number", then the loop variable the same
root_cause: grad.rs's reverse sweep of a `for` pops the pass count off the tape as a number into the forward pass's count variable and recomputes the loop variable as m - 1 - k in numbers; with an Int bound both variables are Int in the forward pass. Renaming the popped count fixes the first error; the loop variable needs its forward type, which the AST rewrite does not know.
note: workaround: a number bound, nterms = float(N)

title: `viv export --infer` (vivlang's load) and `viv lint` refused a file that calls an imported def with a keyword argument: "unknown keyword argument", though `viv run` of the same file works
root_cause: Both read the file alone, and the parser learns an imported def's signature from the module texts that import resolution remembers (viv::used_sigs, B274); neither resolved the imports first, so the imported def had no signature and its keyword arguments were refused. Both now resolve the file's imports before reading it alone.
repro: aa.viv: def f(x: Num, a: Num = 2.0) -> Num { return a * x }; bb.viv: from aa import f / def g(x: Num, a: Num) -> Num { return f(x, a=a) }; viv export --infer bb.viv -o out

title: Inside a def, an if-expression whose branches are elements of module-level [Int] arrays (`node = L[node] if N[node] == 1 else R[node]`) is typed a number: "`node` is an Int but is assigned a number"; the same line at the top level types it Int
root_cause: not traced: the parser lifts `a if c else b` into a hidden variable assigned in both branches of an `if` (parser.rs if_expr); inside a def that hidden variable's Int inference does not count an element of a module-level [Int] as an Int, while the top level's does. Workaround in the compiler's output: an if statement.
repro:
L: [Int] = [1, -1]
R: [Int] = [2, -1]
N: [Int] = [0, 1]
def f(n0: Int) -> Int {
    node: Int = n0
    node = L[node] if N[node] == 1 else R[node]
    return node
}
show f(0)

title: A name the top level only reads (`print(nosuch)`, `show x, nan`) compiled to C and wasm as a global holding zero; the interpreter reports `undefined variable`
found_by: ode (lib/ode: `show ..., nan` printed `nan: 0` from the C build)

title: An index that calls a def writing into the indexed array, `v[f(v)]` (f assigns an element or sorts its Arr parameter), panicked the interpreter: "already borrowed: BorrowMutError" (interp.rs); native and wasm read the element after the write
found_by: vivsmith (tools/fuzz, seeds 100815, 101225, 101689 of a 2004-program run), reduced with tools/fuzz/reduce.py
root_cause: The interpreter's Expr::Index read of a real or complex array evaluated the indices inside `flat_index(&a.borrow().shape, ...)`, holding a borrow of the array's RefCell while the index expression ran; a def called from the index that wrote into the same array (arrays alias as parameters) took borrow_mut and panicked. The shape is now copied out before the indices are evaluated.

title: An Int unpacked from a multiple return (`a, b = f(z)`) becomes a number after `b = b % 5`, and passing it to an Int parameter is refused: "argument 1 of `f` should be an Int but is a number" (`b = b + 1` keeps it an Int)
found_by: vivsmith (tools/fuzz/vivsmith.py, seeds 13 and 19), reduced with tools/fuzz/reduce.py
root_cause: lower.rs infer_expr typed `a % b` and `a // b` as a number as soon as either operand's type was unknown; the unpacked `b = t._1` is unknown until the multiple return's record learns its field types, so the first fixpoint pass fixed b as a number and nothing revised it (`+` waited for both operand types). `%` and `//` now wait too.

c, d = f(b)

title: `int(x)`, `len(a)` and integer literals are Ints only where an Int is expected: `abs`, `min` and `max` of them, and a multiple-return slot holding `int(x)`, are numbers (`m: Int = abs(int(x))` refused; `m: Int = abs(k)` for k: Int accepted)

title: `m: Int = int(g(x)) - (k if c else k)` (k: Int, g a def) is refused: "`m` is an Int but is assigned a number"; with int(x) of a variable, or the if-expression first assigned to a name, it compiles

root_cause: surface.rs `early`: an operand with effects left of a lifted if-expression is computed first into a hidden variable, `viv__eN = int(g(x))`, to keep Python's order. The hidden variable is a number (infer_int_vars skips viv__ names, and `int` adapts only where it stands in an Int position), so the adapting int(...) no longer adapts and Int - number is a number. Candidate fixes: hoist only the effectful argument (`viv__e = g(x)`, then `int(viv__e)` in place), which moves a NaN stop of int() after the if-expression's effects; or type the hidden variable Int as `n = int(...)` is.

title: Appending to an [Int] or Arr that arrived as a parameter and returning it traps in wasm ("error: unreachable") once the array passes about 64 elements; the interpreter and C give the right length
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: The wasm runtime's grow_room sized a COPY by the old block's capacity word, which vrt_seal keeps (it clears only the unsealed flag; the C runtime's seal zeroes the capacity). A parameter is sealed on entry, so every call copied into a block twice the previous capacity: the block doubled per call until the allocation failed and the module trapped. A copy is now sized by the elements (interp/wasm_rt.rs grow_room).
note: Also through a record: `t = s; t.xs = append(t.xs, v); return t` with xs: [Int]. Arrays of records and [Str] grow fine. lib/rv32/asm.viv grows only arrays local to the def. Seen with the 2026-10-11 release viv and the 2026-10-13 .merge build, and viv.wasm builds of 10-13.

title: An empty [Str] in a record literal is refused by the interpreter ("field `names` of `R` is a list of strings but this value is an array"); the C engine builds and runs it
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: The interpreter evaluates `[]` as an empty real array, and its record literal and field assignment converted that only to an empty array of records. Both now convert it to an empty list of strings or Int array where the field has that type (interp.rs empty_as).
note: Also with `names: []` directly. B207 (fixed) was the same family for `in`. Workaround in lib/cc and lib/rv32: ["x"][:0].

title: A slice bound must be a number: s[a:b] with a, b: Int is refused ("expected a number for a slice bound") though an Int indexes directly and features ints-and-numbers says Ints go where numbers go
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: lower/strings.rs's slice of a string or list of strings required a number for each bound and did not convert an Int, as an index does. An Int bound now goes through ints::to_num (exact, or the program stops).
repro:

a: Int = 1
b: Int = 3
show s[a:b]

title: [Int] lacks array operations Arr has: extend ("`extend` joins two real vectors"), sum ("`sum` takes a real array"), and slicing ("only an array can be sliced"), so joining, totaling or copying Int arrays takes a loop
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: Never implemented for [Int]. Added: extend of two Int arrays, slices (read and write), sum (exact, stops on overflow), min and max (stop on an empty array) and sort, in the interpreter (interp.rs, interp/ints.rs, slices.rs, growable.rs), C (fragment int_arr_ops, lower/ints.rs: extend and slices are the real versions on the same 8-byte slots) and wasm (vrt_iextend, vrt_igetslice, vrt_isetslice, vrt_isum, vrt_iminv, vrt_imaxv, vrt_isort).

b: [Int] = [3]

title: A test block that calls stop prints `PASS <name> (no assertions)` and then the stop's error; the exit status is 1, so scripts that read the status still fail, but the PASS line is wrong
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: The interpreter's Stmt::Test ran test_end whatever the block's result, and with no assertion counted it printed PASS before the error went up. Now an error inside a test prints `FAIL <name> -- an error stopped the program` in every engine: the interpreter's test_stopped, the wasm runtime's fail(), and in C a hook (embed.c viv_fatal_hook) that every run-time error's flush of stdout calls while a test runs.
note: Found when a C program in lib/cc/tests/corpus.viv hit a lexer error.

title: A Viv variable named `asm` is emitted as-is by the C backend; `asm` is a C keyword, so the generated C does not compile ("expected 'volatile', 'inline', 'goto', or '('")
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: knotkit's is_reserved_c_ident listed the C89/C99/C11 keywords but not C23's or the extension keywords GCC and Clang accept in their default gnu modes (`asm`, `typeof`, `fortran`) or the predefined lowercase macros (`unix`, `linux`, `i386`). Added, with `noreturn`. Wasm names locals by index and needs nothing.
repro:
asm = "x"
show asm
note: The interpreter and wasm run it. Renamed in lib/cc/codegen.viv's test.

title: A module with only defs and records (no test blocks, no top-level statements) does not link as a C program ("Undefined symbols: _main"), so tools/three-engines.sh reports DOES NOT BUILD for it
found_by: ccviv branch (a C compiler, assembler and RV32IM simulator in Viv)
root_cause: lower.rs adds the Main root only when the top level has statements, and the C backend writes `int main` only for a Main. A new CEmit hook, always_main (true for Viv), makes knotkit write an empty `int main(void)` when there is none; `viv export` renames it as it renames any main.
note: lib/cc/parser.viv and codegen.viv got test blocks (useful anyway).

title: A def named `index` exported through vipyr (`viv export --infer`) runs libc's index() from strings.h instead of the def: the C backend emits the def as `index_`, and the exported entry called it as `index`
root_cause: export_kernels.rs wrote each entry's call with the def's Viv name; knotkit's escape_ident renames a def whose name is reserved in C (index is, since B052), so the call reached the libc function of that name. The entry now calls escape_ident(name), now public in knotkit. The reserved list also takes in the rest of the C library's functions in the headers the runtime includes (stdio.h, stdlib.h, string.h, time.h, stdarg.h: strcmp, memset, fopen, time, clock, ...), so a def or variable of one of those names is renamed too.
note: viv export --infer on the repro, then call index(np.array([4, 5, 6])) from the wrapper: 4 now; before, the call went to strings.h's index with the array's struct as arguments.

title: A def's local `t` takes the type of a top-level variable `t` (a loop variable or an assignment, after the def or in a test block), even when the def is in another module: `t = n` with n an Int becomes a number, and `ts: [Int] = [t]` is refused
note: Refused with "an Int is needed here, and this is a number" at [t]. Without the loop it compiles. The same with `t = 0.5` at the top level instead of the loop, and across modules: the def in modq.viv, `from modq import use` and a test block with `for t to 3` in the main file (a module's def cannot see the importer's globals, so that case is wrong in any reading). Not yet looked into: the guess is that a def's locals are typed against the merged program's global table.

title: The exported skyrmehf library's peak memory grows with repeated runs (about 8 MB per 30 default runs, linear or Pulay mixing), so tools/export/test_skyrmehf.py's test_repeated_runs_give_the_same_bits_and_do_not_grow fails its 4 MB bound (26 MB on main at a7a0901c, 6 MB with Pulay)
repro:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'target/export/skyrmehf')
import skyrmehf as s, resource
for _ in range(3): s.run()
p0 = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
for _ in range(30): s.run()
print((resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss - p0) >> 20, 'MB')
note: The same growth at ab52c363 (before lib/scf was merged), exported with the compiler of a7a0901c, so it is not the SCF loop's. The bits do not change. The test is not in the gate (tools/export_ci.sh runs the export's generated test_skyrmehf.py, not tools/export/test_skyrmehf.py), which is how it went unseen. Not looked into: KEEP_ACROSS_RUNS or a record's arrays outliving the run's arena are the places to start.

title: The reference page said `viv features` lists 181 features written up in 9 areas; the CLI prints 182, because the page counted its own list after leaving out the local-only code-viewer entry and credited that count to the CLI
